item.title: Doctor on why she was immediately skeptical of Elizabeth Holmes' Theranos claims
item.description: Dr. Courtney Lawrence, a board-certified blood donation and transfusion doctor, shared her thoughts on Elizabeth Holmes' now-defunct company Theranos and its promise to transform complex blood testing. Lawrence shared why she was immediately skeptical of the concept with Norah O'Donnell on "Healthful."

item.title: Nashville airport one step closer to being renamed for Dolly Parton
item.description: The Metro Nashville Airport Authority board voted 6-0 on Friday to begin the process of changing the name and said a final name has not been chosen.

item.title: 25 years after 9/11 attacks, America reflects and remembers
item.description: Four former presidents were at the World Trade Center memorial site for 9/11 commemorations, while President Trump spoke at the Pentagon.

item.title: CIA declassifies dozens of never-before-seen 9/11 documents
item.description: The CIA released 71 reports from the months and years leading up to 9/11, providing a new look at what the spy agency told two presidents before the deadly strikes.

item.title: Diesel hits record $6 a gallon as Iran-backed Houthis take key Red Sea territory
item.description: The moves by the Houthis make it easier for the Iran-backed rebels to target ships transiting the crucial Bab el-Mandeb Strait for Saudi Arabian oil exports.

item.title: CBS News correspondent recounts being at Pentagon on 9/11
item.description: Longtime CBS News national security correspondent David Martin arrived at the Pentagon on Sept. 11, 2001, around 10 minutes after a plane crashed into the building. Martin joins to reflect on that day 25 years later.

item.title: Joe diGenova resigns from DOJ after overseeing "grand conspiracy" probe
item.description: Joe diGenova, the prosecutor who was tapped by Attorney General Todd Blanche to supervise the "grand conspiracy" investigation targeting Obama- and Biden-era officials, told CBS News he has resigned.

item.title: How 9/11 changed the American presidency
item.description: George W. Bush said that he instantly became a wartime president after the attacks on Sept. 11, 2001. Presidential historian Doug Brinkley reflects on how America and the role of the chief executive have changed since that day.

item.title: GOP Rep. Rob Bresnahan campaigns on data center limits while investing in industry
item.description: According to a financial disclosure, the Pennsylvania lawmaker holds investments in companies positioned to benefit from the data center industry's continued growth.

item.title: See how your income tax bracket could change for 2027
item.description: The adjustment could provide financial relief for taxpayers who find that more of their income is taxed at lower rates, a Bloomberg analysis suggests.

item.title: Inside the backlash against Kevin O'Leary's massive Utah data center project
item.description: The Stratos project, which could become the biggest data center campus in the United States, is facing backlash from residents of the Utah county where it's being built. CBS News reporter Riley Callanan has more.

item.title: How lower-paid workers are getting their biggest pay raise in years
item.description: Some workers are seeing stronger wage growth by switching jobs, while others are "job-hugging" because of AI, research shows.

item.title: Diesel prices in U.S. top $6 a gallon for first time ever
item.description: The price of diesel has soared more than 60% over the last year, a surge energy experts say is likely to continue. Here's why.

item.title: Teacher explains how she learned to frame lessons for students about 9/11
item.description: Nancy Re, a New York teacher who learned to compose lessons for students about the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, joins CBS News to discuss how she approaches the subject.

item.title: The biggest real-world risks of AI as researchers warn about rapid growth
item.description: A number of tech insiders have voiced concerns and given dire warnings in recent days about the rapid growth of AI. CBS News' Jo Ling Kent and Maya Blackstone have more.

item.title: Remembering 9/11, 25 years later | CBS News Special Report
item.description: It has been 25 years since the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001. Tony Dokoupil and Norah O'Donnell anchor this CBS News Special Report on the commemorations at memorials in New York, Shanksville, Pennsylvania, and the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia.

item.title: Watch: Sixth moment of silence in NYC at 10:28 a.m. when the WTC North Tower collapsed on 9/11
item.description: There was another moment of silence at 10:28 a.m. ET, the moment when the North Tower collapsed at the World Trade Center in New York City on September 11, 2001, 25 years ago.

item.title: Summer music highlights of 2026
item.description: Summer is the time to enjoy live music, indoors and out. Scroll through our gallery of some of 2026's leading musical acts, featuring images by CBS News photojournalist Jake Barlow and photographers Ed Spinelli and Kirstine Walton.

item.title: Saudi Arabia's MBS told Trump to strike Houthis in Yemen, sources say
item.description: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman personally pressed President Trump to take military action against the Iran-backed Houthis as the group advanced rapidly along Yemen's Red Sea coast, two sources say. CBS News' Natalie Brand, Aaron MacLean and Chris Livesay have more.

item.title: Fed rate hike likelihood jumps to nearly 90% after hotter CPI report
item.description: Investors believe the Fed will raise borrowing costs as it works to tame inflation, which has risen a full percentage point since the Iran war started.

item.title: Watch: Trump and Hegseth speak at the Pentagon's 9/11 memorial ceremony
item.description: President Trump, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice spoke at a 9/11 memorial ceremony at the Pentagon 25 years after the Sept. 11, 2001.

item.title: Ross Fire still burning, with over 90,000 acres scorched
item.description: The wildfire, which has torn through Palo Pinto and Jack counties, forced evacuations, closed roads and disrupted schools.

item.title: Suspects in $6 million romance scam targeting women extradited to U.S.
item.description: The men, who were arrested in the South African city of Cape Town in 2021, are set to be handed over to officials from the FBI.

item.title: Have $10,000 to put into a 3-year CD? Here's how much interest you could earn now
item.description: Locking up $10,000 for three years could generate a sizable return at today's top CD rates. Here's what to expect.

item.title: Record-setting cyclospora outbreak is over, U.S. health officials say
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said there is no longer a risk of people getting sick with cyclosporiasis from this outbreak and is confident that all related iceberg lettuce is off the market.

item.title: Watch: Third and fourth moment of silence in NYC and timeline of 9/11 attacks
item.description: At 9:59 a.m. ET on Sept. 11, 2001, the South Tower collapsed at the World Trade Center in New York City during a series of terrorist attacks that changed the U.S. forever. At 10:03 a.m. ET, the passengers on United Airlines Flight 93 launched a counterattack on the hijackers aboard their plane, causing a crash into a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania. It's believed the aircraft may have been headed toward Washington, D.C.

item.title: CPI rose at 3.4% pace in August, raising odds of Fed rate hike this month
item.description: The report comes at a pivotal moment for the Federal Reserve, which is scheduled to meet next week to decide whether to hike interest rates.

item.title: Anthropic says scientists used AI for possible biological weapons development
item.description: Anthropic said it blocked scientists who used its Claude AI models "in ways that could support biological weapons development."

item.title: White House framework for testing new AI models remains hidden as concerns mount
item.description: The White House has not publicly released the voluntary framework for testing frontier AI models that it finalized in August.

item.title: Appeals court declines to lift block on Postal Service rule for mail ballots
item.description: A federal appeals court denied the Trump administration's request to lift a lower court's order that blocked new rules for mail ballots before the midterms.
